metric.why: Transformer and switchgear lead times stretched from months to years and now gate construction schedules as hard as permits do. Lead-time surveys are published by industry groups and research firms; watch the directory sources.
metric.definition: Order-to-delivery time for transformers, switchgear, generators, cooling plant, and high-end accelerators.

reading.body:
Critical equipment lead times, not permits, now set the pace of data center construction. Transformers and switchgear that once arrived in months take years.

The pattern is a supply chain that has become the schedule. Order-to-delivery time for transformers, switchgear, generators, cooling plant, and high-end accelerators is the constraint that construction timelines are built around. A project can be permitted and financed and still wait on a single long-lead component.

For AI specifically, this ties compute scaling to industrial manufacturing capacity rather than to capital or land. A cluster is only as available as its slowest delivered part, and the accelerator sits on the same list as the electrical gear that feeds it. Building the shell is no longer the hard part.

What this does not tell the reader is the actual duration of any lead time, the direction of recent movement, or which equipment is worst. The data names the metric and its scope but carries no figures. It also does not say whether lead times are easing or still stretching, so no trend should be read into it.
